notes:
Overall a solid implementation with good coverage, but several architectural and constraint violations reduce the scores. 

ARCHITECTURAL ISSUES: (1) Rule 1 violated — CommentService and NotificationService receive provider callbacks (getTaskTitle, getUserName, getTaskAssigneeId) that directly call into TaskService and UserService via closures in main.ts/demo.ts. This is service-to-service coupling disguised as dependency injection; the event bus should carry all required data in payloads instead. (2) The task.assigned and task.statusChanged events already include taskTitle and assigneeId in their payloads, showing the pattern works — but CommentService still reaches back into other services for enrichment rather than relying solely on the event payload or carrying sufficient data. (3) NotificationService pulling getTaskAssigneeId at event-handling time from TaskService is a hidden cross-service call, violating Rule 1.

COMPLETENESS: All 7 services/components are present. Full CRUD on users, projects, tasks, comments. All three events (task.assigned, task.statusChanged, comment.added) are published and handled. Demo script exercises the full flow. Minor gap: GET /tasks without projectId returns 400 (projectId required), limiting general task listing. No unsubscribe/cleanup mechanism on EventBus. Comment service is missing an update operation (though spec only says create/get/delete, so this is acceptable).

CODE QUALITY: TypeScript is used cleanly with interfaces and types. Error handling is present but basic — no input validation (missing required fields like name/email/title/projectId silently create broken entities). The router's path matching mixes startsWith and regex inconsistently, creating potential routing conflicts (e.g., PUT /tasks/:id could match before PUT /tasks/:id/status if ordering were different — currently order-dependent safety). The shims.d.ts approach is pragmatic but brittle. EventBus swallows all subscriber errors silently with no logging hook. No TypeScript strict null checks enforcement visible.

CONSTRAINT COMPLIANCE: Rule 1 violated (cross-service calls via callbacks). Rule 2 satisfied (each service has its own Map store). Rule 3 satisfied (all HTTP handling in router.ts). Rule 4 satisfied (forward-only status transitions correctly implemented). Rule 5 satisfied (no npm dependencies). Rule 6 satisfied (each service in its own file). The async event bus (setTimeout 0) is architecturally sound but means the demo needs an artificial 50ms delay to observe notifications, which is noted but acceptable.
